headline: Cannabis retailers may apply for special permits in I-40 zone; mixed-use floating zone approved with 35% residential minimum.
summary: Many residents spoke against the cannabis change, citing youth and health concerns. The mixed-use zone applies only to sites of at least 40 acres, and each project would still need its own approval later. Two other applications were moved to December 14.
decisions: Approved a text amendment letting cannabis retailers apply for special permits in the I-40 zone, with preschools and daycare centers added to a list that includes schools.
Approved a new mixed-use floating zone, raising the minimum residential share to 35% and allowing one drive-through.
discussion: Cannabis retailer change: Residents spoke against it, citing youth, health, and driving concerns. Others said the use is legal under state law and already available in nearby towns.
Cannabis tax revenue: Speakers debated how much the town would get from the 3% municipal tax, with estimates from $150,000 to $250,000 a year.

Mixed-use zone heights and setbacks: Members and residents raised concerns about building heights, buffers next to homes, and the setback from Route 68. The approved draft keeps residential buildings at 50 feet.
Residential share of projects: Members said a 25% minimum for housing could leave a project mostly commercial. The approved draft sets the residential minimum at 35%.
Resident requests for notice: Residents asked for a specific plan and notice to nearby property owners. They also asked for noise, lighting, and truck loading rules.

decision_evidence.quote: Mr. Chairman, I'd like to make a motion to approve uh a zoning text amendment for application 504-26 section 6.34 and 4.8.c cannabis retailer ... The text amendment passes.
Mr. Chairman, I'd like to make a motion to approve application 505-26 for section 4.27 mixed use floating zone zoning, zoning text amendment ... Your motion carries.
